title: KT Signal Connector API v1 host frame

proxyGroupId.description: Proxy group identifier (ADR 0001, Phase 4). 'default' is the reserved, always-present group; additional groups are defined by the trusted launcher at connector spawn and are never created over IPC. An omitted proxyGroup means 'default'.

proxyGroup.description: Optional target proxy group for the account being linked; fixed for the life of the link once link.finish succeeds. An unknown group fails with PROXY_GROUP_NOT_FOUND. A pre-Phase-4 connector rejects this field with INVALID_REQUEST (deny_unknown_fields), so hosts must feature-detect via runtime.status first.

accountsUpdateConfigurationParams.description: Update the account's official settings (contract revision 1.46, §4.45, capability account-settings): at least one of readReceipts / typingIndicators / phoneNumberSharingMode / unlistedPhoneNumber must be present; only the provided keys are forwarded upstream and written (official updateConfiguration partial-write semantics — the upstream writes exactly the provided fields, reads the rest back untouched), and an all-fields-satisfied call is an idempotent no-write success. A call with no writable key answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call. phoneNumberSharingMode takes "everybody" | "nobody" (the official AccountRecord PhoneNumberSharingMode values; the old CONTACTS_ONLY has been removed from the official proto and is not accepted). The result is {status: 'saved'} on a definite success. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable).

readReceipts.description: Whether the account sends read receipts. Optional; omitted means no change upstream.

typingIndicators.description: Whether the account sends typing indicators. Optional; omitted means no change upstream.

phoneNumberSharingMode.description: Who may discover the account by phone number: "everybody" or "nobody" (official AccountRecord values; CONTACTS_ONLY is gone from the official proto). Optional; omitted means no change upstream.

unlistedPhoneNumber.description: Whether the phone number is unlisted from discovery. Optional; omitted means no change upstream.

accountsSetProfileParams.description: Write the account's profile (contract revision 1.46, §4.45, capability account-settings): the text face is a full write exactly like the official updateProfile — every upstream write carries the complete profile, so a text key the caller omits is cleared upstream (the desktop always sends the full text face it wants). givenName is required, 1..128 bytes (the official desktop ProfileEditor maxBytes for both name components); familyName ≤ 128 bytes; about ≤ 512 bytes (the official bio byte budget); emoji ≤ 32 bytes, one emoji. avatar has three states: absent = keep the current avatar, a data:image/*;base64, URI with ≤ 10 MiB decoded = replace, explicit null = remove. The result is {status: 'saved'} on a definite success. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: avatar upload failures fold into STORAGE_WRITE_FAILED and the STORAGE_* family passes through verbatim (retryable).

givenName.description: Required profile first name; the full-write anchor (an empty string is INVALID_REQUEST).

familyName.description: Optional profile last name; omitted (or null) clears it upstream — official full-write semantics.

about.description: Optional profile bio; omitted (or null) clears it upstream — official full-write semantics.

emoji.description: Optional single bio emoji; omitted (or null) clears it upstream — official full-write semantics.

avatar.description: Three states: absent = keep the current avatar; a data:image/*;base64, data URI whose decoded size is 1..10485760 bytes (10 MiB, the engine's stated avatar budget, AvatarHelper-scale) = replace; explicit null = remove. The maxLength is the padded-base64 encoding of the ceiling plus a fixed prefix margin — the connector enforces the decoded budget itself and answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call.

accountsSetExpireTimerParams.description: Set or clear the account's disappearing-message default timer (contract revision 1.46, §4.45, capability account-settings) — the official universal timer (AccountRecord.universalExpireTimer). 0 turns it off; a same-value set is an idempotent no-write upstream. Unlike conversations.setExpireTimer this is the account-level default: new conversations inherit it, per-conversation timers stay on conversations.setExpireTimer, and the universal timer carries no expiration-update broadcast (other devices converge through storage sync). expireSeconds is 0..4294967295 (the engine face validates within u32 and the official field is uint32; unlike the per-conversation face there is no signal-cli int counterpart to share a smaller denominator with). The result is {status: 'saved'} on a definite success. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable).

expireSeconds.description: The account-wide default timer in seconds; 0 turns it off.

accountsSetUsernameParams.description: Set or delete the account's Signal username (contract revision 1.59, §4.55, capability username) — the pinned signal-cli updateAccount mutually exclusive group (username XOR deleteUsername; the schema cannot express XOR so both stay optional and the service ladder enforces exactly-one, answering INVALID_REQUEST when both are present or both absent). username grammar is the official desktop shape mirrored fail-closed: nickname [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*, optional discriminator .N all-digits 0-65535 with no 00-leading and a 0-leading form only as exactly two digits, 3..32 characters total (the pinned libsignal bounds, AccountHelper.java:363-364); a bare nickname (no dot) is allowed and lets the server pick the discriminator. The server reserve/confirm remains the authority — a shape-valid but taken username answers UPSTREAM_ERROR (the upstream 'Invalid username: ...' user error, not a structured code). JVM/native modes dispatch updateAccount directly; the kt-engine face has no username method and answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation — engine-batch debt. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: the result projects the upstream write-back {username, usernameLink?} on the set path (the connector's only username read face — there is no local-account username getter in the pinned signal-cli) and {} on the delete path; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Nothing is persisted connector-side; the desktop mirrors from the write-back.

username.description: The full username (nickname plus optional .discriminator) or a bare nickname. The whole-string wire bound is 38 (the 3..32 nickname window plus the separator and the widest discriminator digit run); the grammar below the wire bound — nickname charset, discriminator forms — is enforced connector-side and answers INVALID_REQUEST.

deleteUsername.description: Delete the account's username; mutually exclusive with username.

accountsGetUsernameParams.description: Read the account's own username (contract revision 1.59, §4.55, capability username). Deliberately answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after account resolution in every mode: the pinned signal-cli has no JSON-RPC reader for the local account's username (JsonAccountResponse is a private write-back record inside UpdateAccountCommand; no listAccounts/getAccount face carries the field) — honest engine-surface debt. Display is fed by the accounts.setUsername write-back mirror instead of a live read.

usernameLookupParams.description: Resolve usernames or username-link URLs against the account's own engine session (contract revision 1.59, §4.55, capability username) — the pinned getUserStatus --username face (resolveRecipientByUsernameOrLink, so bare nicknames are not entries). usernames carries 1..20 entries (KT bound for one host frame; the upstream takes an open array), each 1..64 characters, forwarded verbatim. The result projects the upstream array entry-for-entry: {results: [{recipient, number?, username?, uuid?, isRegistered}]} — uuid != null means the entry resolved to a registered account (uuid == null with isRegistered=false is the unregistered face). The upstream CDSI face can rate-limit (RateLimitException) which surfaces as UPSTREAM_ERROR. Read lane. JVM/native modes dispatch getUserStatus directly; the kt-engine face has no username method and answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation — engine-batch debt. The desktop has no lookup UI in this batch: the face is wire-complete for a later batch.

usernames.description: Usernames or username-link URLs to resolve, 1..20 entries.

conversationsListParams.description: Read lane over the local conversation cache; ordered by newest message, page-bounded, cursor-resumable. Contract 1.43 (§4.42): the result includes the linked account's own Note to Self direct conversation — the contacts sync no longer drops the self entry, so its skeleton materializes like any contact's — and every summary row carries isSelf (always-serialized boolean): true exactly for the direct conversation whose peerKey equals the account's own number (number-based, the §4.24 boundary: the own ACI is not queryable upstream, so a UUID-keyed row cannot be marked), false on every other row including groups. The self row's title is raw contact material (the account's own profile name); the desktop localizes the Note to Self title and avatar from isSelf — the connector ships no copy. Contract 1.60 (§4.52): every summary row carries isTerminated (plain bool, present only when true — absent on false, pre-1.60 hosts read byte-identical rows): the group termination flag the 1.53 §4.50 appendix sync capture stores in the kind='group' contacts row, stamped at read time (a group and its contacts row share the stable id; a group with no cache row yet, every direct row, and every pre-1.53 sync row answer absent/false). The desktop forward-target filter consumes it (the official selectors/composable face excludes terminated groups); the receive chain cannot refresh the flag, only the next contacts.sync can, and syncedAt remains the staleness signal. Contract 1.65 (§4.58): every summary row carries messageRequestAccepted (bare always-serialized boolean, the muted/pinned/isSelf discipline — both values are meaningful): the official isConversationAccepted multi-factor derived at read time over the row's stored engine factor trio (mrr_factors_json — {hidden, profileSharing, blocked} the throttled listContacts enrich stamps on its existing round trip, schema version 20; an engine without the flags stamps the probed-absent {}), the message window, and isSelf. Honest per-factor holes never invented (each collapses to inactive, the official default posture): the ACCEPT response stamp (no pinned engine projects the syncMessage.messageRequestResponse face on the JSON-RPC wire — signal-cli only on its plain-text path), messageCountBeforeMessageRequests (official-desktop migration state), and the group factors addedBy/pendingAdminApprovalV2/group profileSharing (no engine read face) — a group row derives accepted from its own outgoing window alone. A desktop consumes the key as authoritative when present and keeps its local window derivation only for pre-1.65 connectors where the key is absent.

messagesSearchParams.description: Contract 1.30: account-wide substring search over stored message bodies. Empty or whitespace-only queries answer an empty page; queries over 128 characters are rejected (INVALID_REQUEST).

messagesSendTextParams.description: Exactly one addressing form must be set: conversationId, or kind+peerKey (peerTitle optional). mentions (contract revision 1.34) is the optional outbound @mention list: at most 64 entries (extras are dropped, the §4.20 receive cap mirrored); number resolves contacts-first with ACI/UUID passthrough — an entry whose number resolves to nothing local is dropped (the official behavior for unresolvable mention addresses), and an empty number fails closed INVALID_REQUEST; start/length are UTF-16 code-unit offsets the caller indexes against its own body (the official BodyRange semantics).

kind.description: Peer target kind; 'contact' and 'direct' both address a direct chat.

peerKey.description: Recipient number/uuid for direct chats, group id for groups.

peerTitle.description: Optional display title used when the peer send creates a new conversation.

text.description: Non-empty text; the service authoritatively enforces at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes.

number.description: The mentioned address: a phone number (resolved against the local contacts cache, digit-suffix rule) or a UUID-shaped ACI (passthrough).

start.description: UTF-16 code-unit offset into the caller's body.

length.description: UTF-16 code-unit length of the mentioned range.

messagesRetryTextParams.description: Contract 1.31: retry one definitively-failed outgoing text by its clientRequestId (the same idempotency key the original send used). The connector rearms the SAME pending row (status 'failed' -> 'pending') and re-dispatches the upstream send rebuilt from the persisted record — a retry never mints a new clientRequestId, so the local history keeps exactly one row per logical message (official resend behavior; the superseded-row duplication of a naive new-id retry cannot occur). Guards: the row must be an outgoing text with a stored clientRequestId in the terminal state 'failed' — 'pending' answers RETRY_IN_FLIGHT, 'unknown' answers RETRY_NOT_ALLOWED (its wire outcome was never settled, so a blind resend could double-deliver; the host must never auto-resend an unknown outcome), incoming/system rows and rows without a clientRequestId answer INVALID_REQUEST, a missing row or conversation answers MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND / CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND. Settlement follows messages.sendText: the response is the SAME MessageRecord (same row id) now 'sent', an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN leaving the row 'unknown', a definite upstream error answers UPSTREAM_ERROR with the row back in 'failed'.

contactsListParams.description: Read lane over the local contacts cache (§6.5: never calls upstream); ordered by (kind, peerKey), page-bounded, cursor-resumable. Contract 1.44 (§4.43): every result row carries isSelf (always-serialized boolean): true exactly for the kind='contact' entry whose peerKey equals the account's own number — the Note to Self entry the 1.43 contacts sync keeps in the cache, so the desktop can render the localized Note to Self title/avatar in the compose list. Number-based by the §4.24 boundary (the own ACI is not queryable upstream, a UUID-keyed row cannot be marked); group rows are never self. The self row's title stays raw material (the account's own profile name); the desktop localizes the presentation from isSelf — the connector ships no copy. Read-time derivation over the row plus the account record: nothing is stored on the cache row, contacts.sync is unchanged, and the page cursor key stays (kind, peerKey). Contract 1.60 (§4.52): every result row carries isTerminated (plain bool, present only when true — absent on false, pre-1.60 hosts read byte-identical rows): the row's own §4.50 appendix termination marker for kind='group' entries; direct rows and pre-1.53 sync rows answer absent/false. The compose face and the conversation face cannot disagree about the same group.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter over title and peerKey; read-only over the local cache.

messagesEditParams.description: Edit one message the linked account itself sent (contract 1.15). Only a local outgoing row in the terminal state 'sent' qualifies: its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp the edit targets via editTimestamp; pending/failed/unknown rows carry no protocol identity and answer MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. Dispatches signal-cli send with editTimestamp; the connector enforces no local edit window — a late edit answers the upstream rejection (UPSTREAM_ERROR). On confirmed success the updated MessageRecord is returned (body replaced, editedAt set, status unchanged); when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined the answer is SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and the local row is unchanged; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector. Targeting is by conversationId only — the target must already exist in the local history. clientRequestId is accepted for host correlation but the connector does not persist it for edits.

text.description: New message body; bounds identical to messages.sendText.

clientRequestId.description: Optional host correlation id; validated but not persisted.

messagesRemoteDeleteParams.description: Remotely delete (Delete for everyone) one message the linked account itself sent. Only a local outgoing row in the terminal state 'sent' qualifies: its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp addressed by the delete; pending/failed/unknown rows carry no protocol identity and answer MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. Best effort upstream semantics (24h window, quoted/replying messages are not removed). Targeting is by conversationId only — the target must already exist in the local history. The result is {status: 'deleted'} when signal-cli confirmed the delete, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

messagesSendReactionParams.description: Send or remove a reaction to one message that already exists in the local history. Targeting is by conversationId only. A local outgoing row qualifies in the terminal state 'sent' (its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp); an incoming row carries the envelope timestamp, so both directions are addressable. The target author follows the row direction: the linked account's own number for outgoing rows, the conversation peer for incoming rows. Rows without a resolvable protocol identity (missing, pending/failed/unknown outgoing, system) answer MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND; a group incoming row persists only a local sender hash, so its author is not resolvable and the request fails with a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'sent'} when signal-cli confirmed the reaction, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it. remove=true removes a previously sent reaction (upstream best effort).

emoji.description: The reaction; a single unicode grapheme cluster of at most 32 UTF-8 bytes, mirroring the pinned signal-cli requirement.

remove.description: True removes a previously sent reaction; the emoji must still identify the reaction to remove.

messagesSendPinMessageParams.description: Pin one message that already exists in the local history (contract revision 1.33; one pinned message per conversation, the official model). Addressing follows the messages.sendReaction model: a local outgoing row qualifies in the terminal state 'sent' (its sentAt is the upstream Signal timestamp); an incoming direct row carries the envelope timestamp; the target author follows the row direction (the linked account's own number for outgoing rows, the conversation peer for incoming direct rows). Rows without a resolvable protocol identity (missing, pending/failed/unknown outgoing, system, group incoming — only a local sender hash is persisted) fail closed: MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND or a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST. Groups address the engine groupId form, direct chats the recipient array. pinDurationSeconds is the optional timed-pin duration: absent or null is the official forever pin, and a value outside 0..4294967295 fails closed with INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'sent'} when the upstream confirmed the pin, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

pinDurationSeconds.description: Optional timed-pin duration in seconds; absent or null means the pin never expires.

messagesSendUnpinMessageParams.description: Unpin one message that already exists in the local history (contract revision 1.33). Same addressing as messages.sendPinMessage, with no duration: the official unpinMessage carries only the target identity. The result is {status: 'sent'} when the upstream confirmed the unpin, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

messagesSendAdminDeleteParams.description: Remove one message from a group conversation as a group admin (contract revision 1.33; the official deleted-by-admin tombstone). Direct chats have no admin concept and answer INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call. Same addressing as messages.sendPinMessage; admin eligibility is not pre-checked — the server is the authority and rejects non-admin attempts, which surface as the upstream error. A group incoming row persists only a local sender hash, so its author is not resolvable and the request fails with a deterministic INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'sent'} when the upstream confirmed the removal, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it.

messagesMarkReadParams.description: Send the upstream read receipt for messages the peers authored (contract revision 1.34; official sendReceipts per-author fan-out, one engine sendReadReceipt per author with that author's timestamps, the engine chunking 100 per envelope). messageIds is optional: absent means every incoming row of the conversation in ascending sentAt order, both forms bounded at 512 (an explicit list beyond 512 is truncated, not rejected). Only incoming rows qualify — outgoing and system rows are skipped; rows whose author cannot be resolved from local data (group rows carry only a local sender hash) are skipped from the fan-out, not an error. The connector does not persist our own read state (the desktop owns its unread state), so the absent form may re-receipt rows the desktop already marked — duplicates are protocol-idempotent for the peer. The result is {status: 'sent'} when every per-author upstream call confirmed, or {status: 'unknown'} when any failed (including an indeterminate outcome); a receipt failure never fails the request and 'unknown' is never retried automatically. Zero eligible rows is a trivial {status: 'sent'} no-op.

messageIds.description: Optional explicit selection; only incoming rows of this conversation qualify, others are skipped.

messagesMarkViewedParams.description: Send the upstream viewed receipt (contract revision 1.34): identical addressing, selection bounds, per-author fan-out, and {status: sent|unknown} aggregation as messages.markRead, with the engine sendViewedReceipt upstream face.

messageIds.description: Optional explicit selection; only incoming rows of this conversation qualify, others are skipped.

messagesSendViewOnceOpenParams.description: Forward the official view-once open notification (contract revision 1.38): the engine sendViewOnceOpen {account, senderAci, timestamp} face verbatim. Bare passthrough — the desktop flow does not call this directly (messages.markViewOnceOpened orchestrates both legs of the official order); result is receipt-class {status: sent|unknown} and failures degrade to unknown without retry.

timestamp.description: The viewed message's upstream timestamp (ms); 0 carries the official unknown-marker semantics.

messagesMarkViewOnceOpenedParams.description: Burn a viewed view-once message (contract revision 1.38): erase the row body bytes and the connector-owned media files, close open media handles, downgrade the row projection to the viewed placeholder, emit message.viewOnceOpened once, then best-effort orchestrate the official upstream pair (sendViewedReceipt to the author, then sendViewOnceOpen) under receipt-class discipline — failures degrade and are never retried, the burn and the event are unaffected. The desktop's single trigger point for the view-once flow; calling messages.markViewed / messages.sendViewOnceOpen separately is unnecessary (protocol-idempotent if it happens).

messagesReportSpamParams.description: Report conversation messages to the Signal anti-spam pipeline (contract revision 1.49, §4.48, capability report-spam): the engine reportSpam face verbatim — POST v1/messages/report/{senderAci}/{serverGuid} per entry, the server-assigned GUID resolved from the message rows the receive envelopes persisted (schema v17 persistence). The desktop never sees or carries a server GUID. Per-id failures are honest and partial: an id with no row, a NULL-GUID row (pre-1.49 rows or envelopes without the key), or a server rejection enters failures as {messageId, code?} (code = the server's HTTP status when it answered, absent on transport failures) while the rest of the batch still reports; the whole request fails only when the engine reports every GUID rejected (REPORT_SPAM_FAILED, retryable=false). Group conversations answer INVALID_REQUEST (the face reports individual senders; v1 exposes no per-sender selection); a direct peer whose ACI is not resolvable from local data answers INVALID_REQUEST before any upstream call. Zero local writes; the result is the engine projection {reported, failures} verbatim.

conversationId.description: The conversation the messages belong to; direct conversations only (groups answer INVALID_REQUEST).

items.description: A conversation message row id; unresolvable ids fail individually into failures.

messageIds.description: The rows to report; each must belong to this conversation.

messagesAttachmentsOpenParams.description: Open a chunked stream for one already-downloaded attachment (ADR 0002, contract revision 1.17). The (accountId, conversationId, messageId) triple resolves against the store before any file is touched — a bogus conversation or message answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND / MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. The attachmentId must be a bare file name (the id field of the received message's attachment metadata): any id containing '/' or '\\', or any id that resolves to '' / '.' / '..' under the upstream sanitizeId transform ([^A-Za-z0-9_.-] replaced by '_'), answers INVALID_REQUEST before the filesystem is touched, so a hostile id cannot path-traverse. A file signal-cli has not downloaded — or that the media governor already deleted — answers UPSTREAM_ERROR; the two are deliberately indistinguishable. Without the launcher-level --media-ingest opt-in every media method answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. The response is {mediaHandle, sizeBytes, chunkBytes}: mediaHandle is an unguessable 128-bit token bound to this resolved tuple (300 s TTL, at most 8 live handles per account, released early by messages.attachments.closeHandle), sizeBytes is the locally measured file size, and chunkBytes is the raw chunk size (262144) every readChunk offset advances by.

attachmentId.description: The upstream attachment id from the received message's attachment metadata; a bare file name, never a path.

messagesAttachmentsReadChunkParams.description: Read the next chunk of a stream opened with messages.attachments.open (ADR 0002). Offsets are strictly sequential — offset must equal the number of bytes already delivered on this handle — so a handle can never become a random-access scan oracle; any other offset answers INVALID_REQUEST. The response is {dataBase64, sizeBytes, eof}: sizeBytes counts this chunk's raw bytes (at most chunkBytes = 262144; dataBase64 is its padded standard base64, at most 4 * ceil(262144 / 3) = 349528 characters, bounded and far inside the 160 MiB host frame budget) and eof terminates the caller's read loop. A closed, expired, or unknown handle answers INVALID_REQUEST; a file truncated under the stream (media governor pass) terminates with a short chunk and eof; a file that vanished entirely answers UPSTREAM_ERROR.

offset.description: Must equal the bytes already read on this handle; 0 for the first read.

messagesAttachmentsCloseHandleParams.description: Release a media stream before its 300 s TTL (ADR 0002). Idempotent: the response is {released}, false when the handle was already gone (expired or closed earlier). Handles are also released when their account's local data is deleted; the TTL backstops every other kind of abandonment.

messagesSendAttachmentEntry.description: One plural-form attachment (contract revision 1.66): the §4.12 singular budget family per entry — standard padded base64 whose decoded size must equal sizeBytes (1..104857600 bytes), optional filename (1..128 bytes, no path separators or control characters) and optional contentType (type/subtype). No per-entry voice flag: the ;voice=true data-URI parameter is a singular-form face only.

dataBase64.description: Standard padded base64 of the attachment bytes; decoded size must equal sizeBytes.

sizeBytes.description: Declared raw size of this entry; verified against the decoded payload before anything is sent. The entries' combined total stays within the 100 MiB message budget.

filename.description: Optional display filename for the data URI; path separators and control characters are rejected.

contentType.description: Optional RFC 2045 media type 'type/subtype'; defaults to application/octet-stream.

messagesSendAttachmentParams.description: Exactly one addressing form must be set: conversationId, or kind+peerKey (peerTitle optional). Two mutually exclusive payload forms (contract revision 1.66): the singular §4.12 form — dataBase64 is standard padded base64 whose decoded size must equal sizeBytes (1..104857600 bytes, the official Signal attachment ceiling), optional filename (1..128 bytes, no path separators or control characters) and contentType (type/subtype) become data-URI parameters; or the plural §4.59 form — attachments is an array of 1..32 entries (the upstream per-message ceiling), each carrying its own dataBase64/sizeBytes/filename/contentType, and the combined raw payload stays within the same 100 MiB message budget so one request still fits one host frame (the official forward face: one forwarded multi-attachment message is one upstream message). Both forms re-encode payloads as RFC 2397 data URIs for the upstream send call and never persist attachment bytes. The forms are never mixed: any singular key beside the attachments array (or a singular send missing dataBase64/sizeBytes) is INVALID_REQUEST before the pending row exists; voiceNote and viewOnce are singular-form faces and are INVALID_REQUEST on the plural form (a voice note is always a single-attachment message; view-once media is a single unadorned medium). text is an optional caption subject to the sendText byte bound and quoteMessageId quotes one message in the same conversation — shared by both forms. Settlement follows messages.sendText: the response is the sent MessageRecord whose descriptor list carries one entry per attachment in order, and an indeterminate mutating outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with no automatic retry.

kind.description: Peer target kind; 'contact' and 'direct' both address a direct chat.

peerKey.description: Recipient number/uuid for direct chats, group id for groups.

peerTitle.description: Optional display title used when the peer send creates a new conversation.

dataBase64.description: Singular form. Standard padded base64 of the attachment bytes; decoded size must equal sizeBytes. The bound is 4 * ceil(104857600 / 3) — the exact padded-base64 length for the 100 MiB ceiling. Mutually exclusive with the attachments array.

sizeBytes.description: Singular form. Declared raw attachment size; verified against the decoded payload before anything is sent. Mutually exclusive with the attachments array.

filename.description: Singular form. Optional display filename for the data URI; path separators and control characters are rejected. Mutually exclusive with the attachments array.

contentType.description: Singular form. Optional RFC 2045 media type 'type/subtype'; defaults to application/octet-stream. Mutually exclusive with the attachments array.

attachments.description: Plural form (contract revision 1.66): one upstream message carries every entry, the official multi-attachment forward shape. 1..32 entries; the entries' combined sizeBytes stays within the 100 MiB message budget. Mutually exclusive with the singular dataBase64/sizeBytes/filename/contentType keys, and with voiceNote/viewOnce.

text.description: Optional caption; the service authoritatively enforces at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes. Message-level: one caption for the whole send, both forms.

voiceNote.description: Send the attachment as a voice note (contract revision 1.35): the data URI gains ;voice=true (engine maps it to the official VOICE_MESSAGE flag — the exact wire shape the official desktop recorder emits) and the sent descriptor records isVoiceNote. Requires contentType audio/*; anything else is INVALID_REQUEST before the pending row exists. Singular form only: INVALID_REQUEST on the plural attachments array.

viewOnce.description: Send the attachment as a view-once message (contract revision 1.38): the upstream send carries viewOnce=true and the sent row's rich record carries viewOnce so the sender's bubble renders the burn UI across restarts. Requires contentType image/* or video/*, an empty caption, no quoteMessageId, and no voiceNote; any violation is INVALID_REQUEST before the pending row exists. Singular form only: INVALID_REQUEST on the plural attachments array.

messagesSendStickerParams.description: Exactly one addressing form must be set: conversationId, or kind+peerKey (peerTitle optional). Sends one sticker (contract revision 1.35, mirroring the official sendStickerMessage face): packId is the official hex pack id (even length, 1-64 characters), packKey the standard-base64 pack key (1-128 characters), stickerId the pack-local id, emoji an optional ≤32-character label. image follows the messages.attachments.send budget family (dataBase64 standard padded base64, decoded size must equal sizeBytes, 1..104857600 bytes) with one sticker-specific rule: contentType must be image/* (the official client sniffs image MIME and refuses video/text). The upstream send carries only the sticker object — no message body, no regular attachments. The optional quoteMessageId (contract revision 1.37, §4.35) quotes one message in the same conversation: one upstream send carries the sticker object and the quote identity together (the official StagedStickerReply shape); settlement discipline is unchanged. Settlement follows messages.sendText: the response is the sent MessageRecord whose descriptor records the sticker image plus the pack identity, and an indeterminate mutating outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with no automatic retry.

kind.description: Peer target kind; 'contact' and 'direct' both address a direct chat.

peerKey.description: Recipient number/uuid for direct chats, group id for groups.

peerTitle.description: Optional display title used when the peer send creates a new conversation.

quoteMessageId.description: Optional message to quote (contract revision 1.37, §4.35): resolves through the same ladder as messages.sendText — MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id, INVALID_REQUEST when the quoted author is not resolvable — and the upstream send carries quoteTimestamp/quoteAuthor beside the sticker object (the official StagedStickerReply shape). Absent means an unquoted sticker (the 1.35 behavior).

packId.description: Sticker pack id as the official client serializes it: hex, even length (each byte two hex chars), 1-64 characters; passed through verbatim after shape validation.

packKey.description: Sticker pack key in standard base64 (Bytes.fromBase64 convention), 1-128 characters; passed through verbatim after shape validation.

emoji.description: Optional emoji label for the sticker, at most 32 characters.

dataBase64.description: Standard padded base64 of the sticker image bytes; decoded size must equal sizeBytes. The bound is 4 * ceil(104857600 / 3) — the exact padded-base64 length for the 100 MiB ceiling.

sizeBytes.description: Declared raw image size; verified against the decoded payload before anything is sent.

contentType.description: RFC 2045 media type 'type/subtype'; must be image/* (the official client sniffs image MIME and refuses video/text).

width.description: Optional display width, passed through as official AttachmentPointer display metadata.

height.description: Optional display height, passed through as official AttachmentPointer display metadata.

stickerPackManifestParams.description: Fetch one sticker pack's manifest (contract revision 1.36, §4.32): the engine performs the anonymous CDN GET and the official decrypt pipeline (WebAPI.preload.ts fetch, Crypto.node.ts HKDF 'Sticker Pack' → AES-256-CBC+HMAC) — the connector never touches key material beyond passing packKey through, and never persists either field. packId is exactly 32 hex characters (official isPackIdValid — stricter than the 1.35 send projection's ≤64 on purpose); packKey is standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes. Read lane, no account context, no local state. Structured engine errors: STICKER_PACK_KEY_INVALID / STICKER_PACK_FETCH_FAILED / STICKER_PACK_MALFORMED.

packId.description: Sticker pack id, exactly 32 hex characters (official isPackIdValid).

packKey.description: Standard padded base64 of the 32-byte pack key: exactly 44 characters (11 base64 groups, one '=' pad — the only padded encoding whose decode is exactly 32 bytes).

stickerPackImageParams.description: Fetch one sticker's decrypted bytes (contract revision 1.36, §4.32): same pack identity rules as stickerPacks.getManifest plus the pack-local stickerId. The result is {dataBase64, contentType, size} — the decrypted image as standard base64 (≤ 409600 chars: the official 300 KB CDN ceiling plus base64 expansion), its media type, and the decoded byte count. The bytes exist only inside the engine and the response; nothing is persisted. Structured engine errors: the manifest family plus STICKER_IMAGE_TOO_LARGE.

packId.description: Sticker pack id, exactly 32 hex characters (official isPackIdValid).

packKey.description: Standard padded base64 of the 32-byte pack key: exactly 44 characters.

conversationsGetBlockedParams.description: Read the account's blocked conversations (contract revision 1.46, §4.45, capability blocked-conversations): the engine reads the official Storage Service records' blocked bits (per-conversation Contact/GroupV1/GroupV2 records, not the account record) and the result projects {blocked: [{conversationId, kind}]} in storage order — the same entry shape and kind enum as the §4.33 pinned face, capped at 256 entries (KT bound, overflow truncated, entries missing identity or kind drop). Read lane; the connector persists nothing — the cloud record plus the desktop's own cache is the whole story. There is deliberately no blockedAtTimestamp in v1 (matching the engine's registration) and no write counterpart in this batch.

conversationsGetAvatarParams.description: Download one conversation's avatar (contract revision 1.48, §4.47, capability avatar-fetch; engine alignment batch ③a): the engine resolves the conversation reference by shape — an ACI/PNI ServiceId UUID goes straight to the profile face, a phone-number text reverse-resolves through the account's contacts, a 32-byte standard-base64 group master key is the listGroups id form — downloads the encrypted avatar and decrypts it (presage profile/group faces), sniffs the MIME from the magic bytes, and answers {dataUri, byteSize}. The connector resolves the local conversation row first (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call) and forwards the row's peer reference. The result face: dataUri is a data:<mime>;base64, URI (unrecognized magic answers data:application/octet-stream;base64,) whose coarse bound is the engine's 10 MiB decoded cap plus base64 expansion — ≤ 13,981,080 chars, the §4.45 upload schema margin reused as the result guard; this schema length is the coarse envelope, the code enforces the precise decoded budget (decode + byteSize cross-check) and a violation is a protocol error. Read lane, non-mutating; nothing persists — the bytes exist only inside the engine and the response, and neither the bytes nor the URI reach a log line. Structured engine errors: AVATAR_UNAVAILABLE (the honest no-avatar: peer/group has none, profile key never synced, server 403/404 — retryable=false), AVATAR_FETCH_FAILED (network/download/decrypt — retryable=true), AVATAR_TOO_LARGE (beyond the engine's 10 MiB decoded cap — retryable=false); a parameter face the local ladder cannot reach (unknown conversation shape, unregistered account) answers the engine -32603, folded into UPSTREAM_ERROR.

conversationId.description: The conversation to fetch the avatar for; resolved against the account before any upstream call. The engine classifies the reference shape itself (ServiceId UUID / phone number / 32-byte base64 group master key).

conversationsSetBlockedParams.description: Block or unblock one conversation (contract revision 1.48, §4.47, capability blocked-write; engine alignment batch ③a): the engine writes the official storage record's blocked bit with the official storageRecordOps semantics — the first block stamps the engine time, an already-blocked record is idempotent and never rewrites another device's timestamp, unblock clears it — then answers the post-write blocked list {blocked: [{conversationId, kind}]}, the §4.45 conversations.getBlocked result face verbatim (storage order, capped at 256 entries, entries missing identity or kind drop). The connector resolves the local conversation row first (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call) and forwards the resolved peer reference and kind. Blocking never deletes the conversation or its messages (the official desktop behaves the same). Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: CONVERSATION_NOT_RESOLVED (the cloud reference does not resolve — retryable=false) and the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable); no new codes on this face.

conversationId.description: The conversation to block or unblock; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

kind.description: The upstream conversation reference taxonomy: direct chat, GroupsV2 group, or GroupsV1 legacy group.

blocked.description: true blocks the conversation, false unblocks it. Required — there is no toggle form.

callsSendSignalParams.description: Forward one outbound call-signaling frame (contract revision 1.55, §4.49, capability call-signaling): the connector shape-gates the envelope — type against the RingRTC 1:1 frame-family enum, callId a positive integer (u32 face, the legacy frames' id address space), payload mandatory (non-empty, ≤ 3,145,728 chars, the coarse envelope of the same budget the receive face enforces) for the modern faces offer/answer/ice and optional (absent) for the legacy busy/hangup family — the official proto bare frames CallMessage{busy{id}} / CallMessage{hangup{...}} carry no opaque field (RingRTC 2.72.1 emits them opaque-less, verified in the P1 device experiment), so a payload-less busy/hangup routes the engine sendCallMessage legacy face instead of inventing bytes — resolves the local conversation row (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call; direct conversations only, the upstream sendCallMessage face is contact-only and a group shape fails closed) and forwards the signaling payload byte-for-byte as the engine's {account, recipient, data|legacy} upstream face. urgency (1.55) is the optional pass-through wake-up bit forwarded to the engine's CallMessage{opaque{urgency}} (absent = the engine's droppable default). The connector never parses, validates, or logs the signaling content: the engine owns the transport face (Content.callMessage=3, official Signal-Desktop RingRTC behavior aligned, AGPL zero-copy) and the desktop + calling sidecar's RingRTC state machine parses the frames. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: the reaction-class write-lane mutex and delete drain barrier apply; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. The result {sentAt} is the engine's envelope timestamp — a send ack, not call state.

conversationId.description: The direct conversation the signaling addresses; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

type.description: The RingRTC 1:1 frame family the frame carries. offer/answer/ice demand payload (the RingRTC-serialized opaque material); busy/hangup may omit it (the legacy bare-frame family, engine-built from the callId). Gated for the route decision and the desktop-side logging/routing honesty; the payload itself is self-describing.

callId.description: The 1:1 call identity the RingRTC frames share (the legacy frames' id face). Positive u32; 0 is the no-call marker and is rejected.

payload.description: The opaque signaling material (RingRTC-serialized), forwarded byte-for-byte. Mandatory for offer/answer/ice; omit for a legacy busy/hangup bare frame (the engine builds CallMessage{busy{id}} / CallMessage{hangup{id}}). The connector validates the envelope shape only — never the content.

urgency.description: The optional wake-up bit (contract 1.55), forwarded to the engine's CallMessage{opaque{urgency}}. Absent = the engine's droppable default (proto: a missing urgency treats as DROPPABLE). Only meaningful with a payload (the legacy bare frames have no opaque envelope).

callsGetStateParams.description: Read the connector's call-state registry (contract revision 1.51, §4.49, capability call-signaling): account-scoped, repeatable, store-only — no engine call, no network. The honest projection: the connector is the signaling pipe between the engine's transport and the desktop + calling sidecar's RingRTC state machine; it persists no call state, so the registry reads {calls: [], projection: "connector-pipe"} — the stable face a later batch fills if the connector ever learns to register state. Read lane.

conversationsGetPinnedParams.description: Read the account's pinned conversations (contract revision 1.36, §4.33): the engine reads the official Storage Service AccountRecord.pinnedConversations and the result projects {pinned: [{conversationId, kind}]} in cloud order — array order is the pin order, there are no timestamps. Read lane. The connector persists nothing: the host pulls at startup/refresh (poll-on-open, no live push on this face).

conversationsSetPinnedParams.description: Pin or unpin one conversation (contract revision 1.36, §4.33): the engine writes the official storage record (the same path the official desktop uses). conversationId resolves through the local store (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call); the result is the post-write cloud state {pinned: [...]} read back — not a local echo. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: CONVERSATION_NOT_RESOLVED (the cloud reference does not resolve) and the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim. Message-level pins (messages.sendPinMessage, §4.28) are an orthogonal concept — this face pins conversations, not messages.

conversationId.description: The conversation to pin or unpin; wider than the opaqueId family because the host may address a conversation not yet materialized locally. Resolved against the account before any upstream call.

kind.description: The upstream conversation reference taxonomy: direct chat, GroupsV2 group, or GroupsV1 legacy group.

pinned.description: true pins the conversation, false unpins it. Required — there is no toggle form.

messageRequestParams.description: Accept or decline one conversation's message request (contract revision 1.63, §4.56, capability message-requests): the two methods ride the pinned upstream's native sendMessageRequestResponse sync face — accept = type accept, decline = type delete (the official CLI carries only the accept/delete pair; the block and block-and-delete twins are the desktop's explicit conversations.setBlocked compositions). Direct conversations forward the resolved peer reference (recipient), groups the raw group master key (groupId). The pinned face answers an empty result object on success and folds per-recipient failures into an unstructured USER_ERROR, so the result face is {status} only. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Zero local writes: the request state converges through the §4.56 receive projection.

conversationId.description: The conversation whose request is being answered; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

conversationsSetExpireTimerParams.description: Set or clear one conversation's disappearing-message timer (contract revision 1.42, §4.41; group conversations since 1.45, §4.44): a direct conversation follows the connector's engine mode — the engine face's setExpirationTimer {account, recipient, expirationInSeconds} or the signal-cli face's updateContact {account, recipient, expiration} (int seconds); a group conversation (1.45) routes updateGroup {account, groupId, expiration} in every mode — the §4.41 'group timers are unreachable' boundary is overturned (the upstream parameter is named expiration), and the 2026-10-06 dated note lifted the last mode gate after the engine batch landed updateGroup {expiration} (engine main @ 216a4c7; GROUP_UPDATE_FAILED carries data.status from the server rejection honestly). Same-value sets are upstream no-ops (no broadcast, no version bump — official semantics); 0 turns the timer off; there is no toggle form. conversationId resolves through the local store (CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND before any upstream call). The receive side converges the same mirror: the engine's groupUpdated {groupId, revision, expireTimerSeconds, editor?} projection (0 = off) updates conversations.expire_timer_seconds and rides conversation.changed — state convergence only, no message row, and the desktop presentation for group timer changes is a later batch (2026-10-06 dated note). Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. On success the local conversation mirror updates and the refreshed summary rides conversation.changed; the result is {expireTimerSeconds: n}. Note the engine face validates recipient against registered contacts — an unregistered peer answers the upstream error verbatim (fail-closed UPSTREAM_ERROR family).

conversationId.description: The direct conversation to set the timer on; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

expireSeconds.description: The timer in seconds: 0 turns disappearing messages off; N counts down every message in the conversation from its own send/start time. Bounded by the shared upstream int face (i32::MAX).

stickerPackGetSyncsParams.description: Read the account's sticker-pack sync records (contract revision 1.37, §4.34): the engine reads the official Storage Service StickerPackRecord set — installed packs carry packId + packKey + position, uninstalled packs a deletedAtTimestampMs tombstone. The result projects {packs: [...]} in cloud order, capped at 256 entries (KT bound, overflow truncated, entries missing packId dropped). Read lane; the connector persists nothing — the cloud record plus the desktop's own cache is the whole story.

stickerPackSetSyncParams.description: Install or uninstall one sticker pack for the account (contract revision 1.37, §4.34): installed=true requires packKey (standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes) and optionally positions the pack; installed=false writes the deletedAtTimestampMs tombstone and ignores packKey/position. The result is the post-write cloud state {packs: [...]} read back — not a local echo. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Structured engine errors: the STORAGE_* family passed through verbatim (retryable); no new codes are introduced by this face.

packId.description: Sticker pack id, exactly 32 hex characters (the §4.32 browse-face shape, aligned with the official isPackIdValid).

packKey.description: Pack key in standard base64 decoding to exactly 32 bytes (44 padded characters); required when installed is true, ignored (forwarded as null) otherwise.

installed.description: true installs the pack (packKey required), false uninstalls it (tombstone write). Required — there is no toggle form.

position.description: Optional cloud ordering position for an installed pack; u32 range. Ignored when installed is false.

groupsGetParams.description: Read-only projection (contract revision 1.9, roster added in 1.40, isTerminated added in 1.53, requestingMembers added in 1.62, pendingMembers added in 1.64) of the local contacts cache for one group: {peerKey, title, memberCount?, members?, isTerminated, requestingMembers?, pendingMembers?, syncedAt}. Served from the rows written by contacts.sync — the connector never calls the upstream for the cached face, so an unsynced or departed group (the sync filters isMember=false) answers GROUP_NOT_FOUND; syncedAt lets the host judge staleness itself. members (contract 1.40, §4.39) is the bounded roster the sync captured (cap 1001, the official GroupsV2 group-size ceiling): entries carry id (the connector-wide number-before-uuid address ladder), optional uuid (only when the upstream supplied one), optional name (resolved at read time from the same account's contacts cache; absent when unknown), self (true when id is the linked account's number; absent otherwise), and admin (only when the upstream marks the member — absent on engines without an admin face). Rows synced before 1.40 carry no members key. isTerminated (contract 1.53, §4.50 appendix) is the upstream JsonGroup.isTerminated flag as of the row's last sync, projected as a plain bool — false for pre-1.53 rows and engines without the flag; the receive envelope (JsonGroupInfo) exposes no terminated field, so only the next sync refreshes it and syncedAt remains the staleness signal. requestingMembers (contract 1.62, §4.53 appendix) is the one live face of this method: the same single-group upstream listGroups read the 1.58 approval fold runs against, projected to bounded entries {id (the first-wins address ladder — either identity folds), uuid?, name?}; present only when the engine answered with a non-empty requesting set, absent otherwise (the engine is stopped, the upstream face is missing, or nobody is requesting — the desktop renders no approval section). The key is deliberately NOT a sync-captured cache field: the approval truth source is the fold's own live read (the 1.58 record), and one source keeps the rendered list and the folded write set from ever disagreeing; freshness is the read call itself, which also lets the desktop's post-action refresh observe the converged list without waiting for contacts.sync. pendingMembers (contract 1.64, §4.57, capability group-invite-revoke — one capability for the read and write halves) is the same-shaped live read of the invited-but-not-yet-joined set: the same single-group listGroups read the §4.57 revoke fold runs against, projected to bounded entries {id, uuid?, name?}; present only when the engine answered a non-empty pending set, absent otherwise. The upstream face carries no inviter metadata (JsonGroupMemberAddress has no addedByUserId), so no invited-by grouping rides this face — the official PendingInvites panel groups rows by inviter, a recorded projection difference. Metrics classify it as contacts; no event is emitted.

groupKey.description: The upstream group id, exactly the peerKey of the cached kind='group' contacts row.

groupsUpdateParams.description: Apply one group-management change set to one group conversation (contract revision 1.45, §4.44, capability group-management). The change keys are individually optional and mirror the pinned signal-cli updateGroup jsonRpc surface verbatim: name (from groupName), description (from groupDescription), members (from addMembers), removeMembers, admins (from promoteAdmins), removeAdmins (from demoteAdmins), bans (from banMembers), unbans (from unbanMembers), resetLink, link (from linkState: the connector's enabled-without-approval maps to the upstream choice 'enabled'), setPermissionAddMember / setPermissionEditDetails / setPermissionSendMessages (every-member | only-admins), memberLabel, memberLabelEmoji. At least one change parameter must be present (an empty change set answers INVALID_REQUEST; resetLink=false counts as absent). An empty member array is INVALID_REQUEST — upstream reads absence as 'no change' and an explicit empty set would commit a no-delta group change broadcast. Member arrays carry at most 1001 entries (the official GroupsV2 ceiling), each 1-128 chars, forwarded verbatim (the upstream resolves and rejects unknown addresses). groupName/memberLabel 1-256 bytes, groupDescription up to 4096 bytes, memberLabelEmoji one emoji grapheme cluster (<=32 bytes). conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any upstream call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST). Group avatar is not exposed: upstream takes a local file path and the connector has no host-file upload channel (recorded boundary). JVM/native modes dispatch updateGroup directly; the kt-engine face has no updateGroup method and answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation — engine-batch debt. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Group state converges through the receive projection: a bodyless groupInfo type=UPDATE envelope lands as a system row (rich marker isGroupUpdate) and conversation.changed carries the mirrored title.

conversationId.description: The group conversation to update; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

promoteAdmins.description: Members to promote to admin; upstream key 'admins'.

linkState.description: Group invite-link state; upstream key 'link'. The connector's enabled-without-approval maps to the upstream choice 'enabled'.

resetLink.description: Reset the group link and create a new link password; upstream key 'resetLink'. false carries no change semantics (absent).

permissionAddMember.description: Who may add members; upstream key 'setPermissionAddMember'.

permissionEditDetails.description: Who may edit group details; upstream key 'setPermissionEditDetails'.

permissionSendMessages.description: Who may send messages; upstream key 'setPermissionSendMessages'.

memberLabel.description: The group's member label string; upstream key 'memberLabel'.

memberLabelEmoji.description: The group's member label emoji: exactly one unicode grapheme cluster of at most 32 UTF-8 bytes; upstream key 'memberLabelEmoji'.

groupsQuitParams.description: Leave one group conversation (contract revision 1.45, §4.44, capability group-management): the upstream quitGroup {account, groupId} write. conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any upstream call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST). The upstream --delete local-data flag and the --admin last-admin handoff list are deliberately not exposed: the official client keeps the conversation as a non-member after leaving, and a last-admin quit without a handoff answers the upstream UserErrorException verbatim (UPSTREAM_ERROR family). JVM/native modes dispatch quitGroup directly; the kt-engine face has no quitGroup method and answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation — engine-batch debt. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. The local conversation row is kept (non-member state is upstream convergence, like groups.update).

conversationId.description: The group conversation to leave; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

groupsTerminateParams.description: Terminate one group conversation for every member (contract revision 1.52, §4.50, capability group-terminate): the upstream terminateGroup {account, groupId} write — the pinned 0.14.8 JSON-RPC face (TerminateGroupCommand, a JsonRpcLocalCommand) wrapping GroupHelper.terminateGroup → GroupV2Helper.terminateGroup → libsignal createTerminateGroup(). conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any upstream call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST). Upstream requires admin privileges; a non-admin answers the GroupsV2 UNAUTHORIZED face and a v1 group answers the v1-only refusal — both forward verbatim as the UPSTREAM_ERROR family, never invented locally. The action is irreversible on the Signal service: afterwards nobody can send messages or start calls in the group, and members keep read access to the existing history (official “End group” behavior anchors). JVM/native modes dispatch terminateGroup directly; the kt-engine face is the pinned engine's gap and answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Zero local writes: the terminated state converges through the group-update receive projection (§4.44).

conversationId.description: The group conversation to terminate; resolved against the account before any upstream call.

groupsApproveJoinRequestsParams.description: Approve or refuse one group's pending join requests (contract revision 1.58, §4.53, capability group-join-approve): members carries the candidate member set (1-1001 entries of 1-128 characters, the §4.39 roster bounds; an empty array is refused — it carries no change upstream), approve=true approves the join requests, approve=false refuses them. The upstream write is the pinned 0.14.8 updateGroup face (GroupHelper.updateGroupV2 weaves approval into the member semantics: members entries that are requesting members ride approveJoinRequestMembers, removeMembers entries that are requesting members ride refuseJoinRequestMembers). Because those shared arrays would otherwise add or remove ordinary members, the connector folds the candidates against the engine's own requesting-members read (listGroups → JsonGroup.requestingMembers) before anything goes upstream — only candidates the engine still reports as requesting can ride the arrays, so a stale or mistaken candidate fails closed at the connector instead of adding or removing a member. A fold that empties the candidate set answers JOIN_REQUEST_NO_LONGER_PENDING (retryable — the request was resolved elsewhere); a candidate rejected upstream (non-admin) forwards verbatim as the UPSTREAM_ERROR family. conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any engine call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST, unknown answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND). JVM/native modes dispatch the fold + updateGroup directly; the kt-engine face answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Zero local writes: the roster converges through contacts.sync.

conversationId.description: The group conversation whose join requests are being decided; resolved against the account before any engine call.

members.description: The candidate member set (the members' numbers or uuids as the caller read them); duplicated entries collapse. Each entry must still be requesting membership at the engine or it drops from the write (fail closed).

approve.description: true approves the join requests (the members ride the upstream members family); false refuses them (the removeMembers family).

groupsRevokeInvitesParams.description: Revoke one group's pending invitations (contract revision 1.64, §4.57, capability group-invite-revoke): members carries the candidate member set (1-1001 entries of 1-128 characters, the §4.39 roster bounds; an empty array is refused — it carries no change upstream). The upstream write is the pinned 0.14.8 updateGroup removeMembers family (GroupHelper.updateGroupV2 discriminates three ways: entries that are pending members ride revokeInvitedMembers, entries that are full members ride the member removal, entries that are requesting members ride refuseJoinRequestMembers). Because that shared array would otherwise remove an ordinary member or refuse a join request, the connector folds the candidates against the engine's own pending-members read (listGroups → JsonGroup.pendingMembers) before anything goes upstream — only candidates the engine still reports as pending invitees can ride the array, so a stale or mistaken candidate fails closed at the connector instead of removing a member or refusing a request. A fold that empties the candidate set answers INVITE_NO_LONGER_PENDING (retryable — the invite was resolved elsewhere: another admin revoked it, the invitee joined); a candidate rejected upstream (non-admin) forwards verbatim as the UPSTREAM_ERROR family. conversationId must resolve to a kind='group' row before any engine call (direct answers INVALID_REQUEST, unknown answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND). JVM/native modes dispatch the fold + updateGroup directly; the kt-engine face answers CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (retryable=false) after local validation. Send lane, account-scoped mutating: result is {status: 'sent'} on a definite success; an indeterminate outcome answers SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never retried. Zero local writes: the roster converges through contacts.sync.

conversationId.description: The group conversation whose pending invitations are being revoked; resolved against the account before any engine call.

members.description: The candidate member set (the invitees' numbers or uuids as the caller read them); duplicated entries collapse. Each entry must still be a pending invitee at the engine or it drops from the write (fail closed).

contactsSetLocalAliasParams.description: Rename one contact as the linked account sees it (contract revision 1.10): the mutating upstream updateContact carries {account, recipient, name}, where recipient is the peer key as a single string (the pinned UpdateContactCommand reads it with getString — an array would fail upstream). peerKey must resolve to a locally known contact (a cached kind='contact' row or a direct conversation peer); anything else answers INVALID_REQUEST. The result is {status: 'updated'} when signal-cli confirmed the rename, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it. No local row is modified: the alias lives in upstream account data and returns through the next contacts.sync; no event is emitted.

peerKey.description: The contact's number/uuid; must already be known to this account.

alias.description: The new display name, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes.

presenceSetTypingMessageParams.description: Send or stop the typing indicator to one conversation (contract revision 1.11). The mutating upstream sendTyping command carries {account, stop, recipient: [peerKey]} for direct conversations or {account, stop, groupId} for groups; the connector always sends the stop boolean explicitly (the null handling of an absent key is not part of the pinned upstream contract), and signal-cli expires the indicator by itself after roughly 15 seconds, so stop=true is an early clear, not a requirement. Targeting is by conversationId only; a missing conversation row answers CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND. The result is {status: 'sent'} when signal-cli confirmed the call, or {status: 'unknown'} when the outcome of the mutating upstream call cannot be determined; 'unknown' is never retried automatically by the connector (host may explicitly re-send with a fresh requestId and the same operationId). operationId is an optional host correlation id; the connector validates its shape but does not persist it. Nothing is written locally and no event is emitted: a typing indicator is ephemeral upstream protocol state, and inbound typing events remain a declared TODO.

stop.description: true stops an active indicator early; false (default) starts one.

historyImportStatusParams.description: Link-time history import status (contract revision 1.39, §4.38; progress extended by revision 1.54): the honest minimal projection of the backup5 archive import (ADR 0005 S3) for the desktop's S4 UI. Read-only over local state — it never touches the network. States: 'pending' (linked inside the link-time wait window, the engine's best-effort archive download has not produced the archive file yet), 'running'/'completed'/'failed' (from the persisted import row with real counters), 'unavailable' with reason 'engine-mode' (signal-cli JVM/native has no backup5 capability) or 'no-archive' (wait window expired with no archive — the engine's failure modes are indistinguishable from 'the phone had nothing to transfer' and are reported as such, never guessed). While state is 'running' the result may carry progress {stage: 'downloading'|'processing', bytesTransferred?, bytesTotal?} — 'downloading' is the engine's transfer-archive byte snapshot (bytes ride together only when the engine read a content-length; otherwise stage alone, never a zero-filled guess), 'processing' is the connector's own NDJSON import pass and never carries byte fields (the official Process stage renders copy, not numbers); pending/completed/failed/unavailable never carry progress, and a malformed engine snapshot drops the object while keeping the state. The desktop polls while state is 'running'; there is deliberately no push event in this revision. Since contract 1.56 (§4.38 attachv2) the import also persists the archive's attachment pointer faces (key material, transit CDN, integrity) into the internal attachment_locators column — never on this wire face; since contract revision 1.57 the history.attachmentDownload face walks those faces end to end (the descriptors stay metadata-only; the bytes land behind messages.attachments.open).

historyImportRetryParams.description: Manually retry one account's failed link-time history import (contract revision 1.54, §4.38, capability history-import): the official failure dialog's Retry action (Signal-Desktop installer.preload.ts retryBackupImport → backupsService.retryDownload, AGPL semantics anchor) mapped onto the connector face. Clears the account's 'failed' ledger row and re-arms the orchestration — with the archive still on the engine face the state returns to 'pending' and the sweep (next engine start) or the link watcher picks it up; attempts keep counting across retries (the ≤3 automatic budget stays supervisor-owned, the manual face is unbounded like the official dialog). Result {armed: true, state: 'pending'}. Errors: shape errors INVALID_REQUEST (retryable=false); a ledger row that is not 'failed' (pending/running/completed) or a JVM/native face answers NOT_RETRYABLE (retryable=false); no importable archive on the engine face (a failed row whose archive vanished, or no row at all with no archive — the download never landed) answers NO_ARCHIVE (retryable=false); unknown accounts answer ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND through the shared store path. Send lane, account-scoped mutating (the reaction-class write-lane mutex and delete drain barrier serialize it against every other account mutation) — no upstream traffic, no engine call in the retry itself.

historyAttachmentDownloadParams.description: Download one imported history attachment's bytes from the Signal transit CDN (contract revision 1.57, §4.38 step 3, capability history-import — no new capability bit, the 1.53 precedent). The attachmentId names one descriptor of the message's received metadata (the messages.attachments.open addressing shape); the connector resolves the message locally, finds the descriptor's stored pointer face (persisted since contract 1.56 in the internal attachment_locators column), and walks the official attachv2 pipeline: cdnNumber → cdn base assembly (the official getCheckedCdnUrl map with the unknown-number fallback to CDN 0, encodeURIComponent'd cdnKey path), streamed GET (connect 10 s / total 120 s / no redirects), the ciphertext gates (trailing-MAC HMAC-SHA256 terminal check, then the whole-body SHA-256 digest face when the locator carries it), AES-256-CBC decryption (IV prefixed to the body, PKCS7), the official log-pad trim to the declared plaintext size, and the plaintextHash face over the trimmed plaintext. The plaintext lands in the governed media directory under the attachment's stable id — afterwards messages.attachments.open/readChunk deliver it exactly like any engine-downloaded file. Both integrity faces verify when both ride; a locator with only plaintextHash is the media-tier face and stays downloadable (the §4.38 ruling: its mismatch is terminal because no digest re-check remains). Fail-closed: a descriptor without a pointer face, a face missing key/cdnKey/cdnNumber/any integrity value, a malformed key or hash, or a missing/out-of-range size answers INVALID_REQUEST before any network traffic. Download, integrity, and decryption failures answer UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=false — terminal, never auto-retried (§4.38 honest degradation; the official tap-to-retry face is a caller action). Local filesystem failures answer UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=true. Already-present files answer {sizeBytes} without touching the CDN (idempotent dedup: an earlier call, or the engine's own live download of the same id). Result {sizeBytes: N} — the plaintext byte count messages.attachments.open will report; no handle, no path: the bytes stay behind the chunked media triple. Send lane, account-scoped mutating (it lands a file in the media directory; the reaction-class write-lane mutex and delete drain barrier serialize it).

attachmentId.description: The attachment id from the message's received metadata (a bare attachment file name; path separators refused).

attachmentDownloadParams.description: Download one message attachment's bytes from the Signal transit CDN (contract revision 1.61, §4.54, capability attachment-download): the on-demand byte channel for message-attachment pills — the caller names the message and the descriptor's positional index, the connector resolves the row locally and walks the stored pointer face through the official attachv2 pipeline (the same machine as history.attachmentDownload, §4.38 step 3: cdnNumber → cdn base map with the CDN-0 fallback, encodeURIComponent'd cdnKey path, streamed GET with connect 10 s / total 120 s / no redirects, trailing-MAC HMAC-SHA256 then whole-body SHA-256 digest gates, AES-256-CBC decrypt with the IV-prefixed body and PKCS7, the official log-pad trim, the plaintextHash face). The pointer face resolves through the locator ladder: the live-receive column first (persisted since this revision in the internal live_attachment_locators column when the engine projects a receive locator — the pinned 0.14.8 signal-cli and the kt-engine receive face project metadata only today, so live rows answer the hole), then the schema-18 import column (the index-aligned archive faces persisted since 1.56). Fail-closed: an index past the descriptor list, or a hole in both locator columns (a descriptor without any pointer face) answers INVALID_REQUEST before any network traffic — never a guessed download. Download, integrity, and decryption failures answer UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=false — terminal, never auto-retried; local filesystem failures answer UPSTREAM_ERROR retryable=true. Already-present files answer {sizeBytes} without touching the CDN (idempotent dedup: an earlier call, or the engine's own live download of the same id). Result {sizeBytes: N} — the plaintext byte count messages.attachments.open will report; no handle, no path: the bytes stay behind the chunked media triple. Send lane, account-scoped mutating (it lands a file in the governed media directory; the reaction-class write-lane mutex and delete drain barrier serialize it).

attachmentIndex.description: The zero-based position of the attachment in the message's received metadata — the descriptor list order the wire row already carries.

backupsExportParams.description: Start the engine's Android local-backup export for the account (contract revision 1.47, §4.46, capability backup-export): the connector (re)builds the transitional NDJSON artifact in the engine's per-account data directory (same directory as the backup5 history-import artifact, resolved through the engine's engine-state.json registry; the engine deletes it when the task leaves running — the engine never persists chat content), then forwards to the engine's backup.export, which runs a dedicated background thread (the receive pipeline stays live throughout). One task per account at a time; a second start answers BACKUP_EXPORT_ALREADY_RUNNING (poll backups.exportStatus instead of retrying). Result {status: 'started'}; progress and the snapshot list come from backups.exportStatus. Caps the connector enforces on its own artifact build: per-line 1048576 bytes, 4000000 lines, 2147483648 bytes total, chat_item body 131072 bytes (mirroring engine backup-export-contract §10.2). Request-frame method enum, dispatch literals, FEATURE_CAPABILITIES tag, and structured-error whitelist registered with the connector implementation batch (implemented 2026-10-06, §4.46 plan).

backupsExportStatusParams.description: Poll the engine's Android local-backup export task (contract revision 1.47, §4.46, capability backup-export): result mirrors the engine honestly — {state: idle|running|completed|failed, artifactPresent, startedAtMs?, finishedAtMs?, lines?, frames?, snapshot?: {name, mainBytes, frames?}, error?, snapshots: [{name, mainBytes, frames?}]} with absent keys omitted rather than zero-filled; snapshots lists at most 32 entries newest-first and the engine only reports, never deletes (cleanup ownership is the connector's: keep the latest snapshot, clear older ones and -tmp residue before the next export).
