Desktops poll while running; deliberately no push event (§4.38 precedent). The task registry is engine-process memory: an engine restart reads idle while on-disk snapshots stay listed. Wire-frame registration landed with the connector implementation batch (implemented 2026-10-06, §4.46 plan); see backupsExportParams.

backupsExportFileOpenParams.description: Open a chunked stream for one file of the latest local-backup snapshot (contract revision 1.47, §4.46, capability backup-export): the media three-chain shape (messages.attachments.open, ADR 0002) reused verbatim — response {fileHandle, sizeBytes, chunkBytes} with chunkBytes 262144, handle TTL 300 s, at most 8 live handles per account, released early by backups.exportFile.closeHandle. file is a two-value enum: only the latest snapshot's fixed file names are addressable — there is no path parameter and the connector never exposes arbitrary paths; 'latest snapshot' is the newest signal-backup-<UTC ts> directory in the account's SignalBackups/ root as reported by backups.exportStatus.snapshots. No snapshot exists yet answers BACKUP_SNAPSHOT_MISSING. Wire-frame registration landed with the connector implementation batch (implemented 2026-10-06, §4.46 plan); see backupsExportParams.

file.description: The fixed snapshot file name; no path component is accepted.

backupsExportFileReadChunkParams.description: Read the next chunk of a snapshot file stream opened with backups.exportFile.open (contract revision 1.47, §4.46, capability backup-export): identical ladder to messages.attachments.readChunk — offsets strictly sequential (offset must equal the bytes already delivered on this handle, so a handle can never become a random-access scan oracle), response {dataBase64, sizeBytes, eof} with sizeBytes at most chunkBytes = 262144 and dataBase64 at most 349528 characters; a closed, expired, or unknown handle answers INVALID_REQUEST; a snapshot removed under the stream (connector cleanup) terminates with a short chunk and eof, a vanished root answers UPSTREAM_ERROR. Wire-frame registration landed with the connector implementation batch (implemented 2026-10-06, §4.46 plan); see backupsExportParams.

offset.description: Must equal the bytes already read on this handle; 0 for the first read.

backupsExportFileCloseHandleParams.description: Release a snapshot file stream before its 300 s TTL (contract revision 1.47, §4.46, capability backup-export): idempotent like messages.attachments.closeHandle — response {released}, false when the handle was already gone. Handles are also released when their account's local data is deleted; the TTL backstops every other kind of abandonment. Wire-frame registration landed with the connector implementation batch (implemented 2026-10-06, §4.46 plan); see backupsExportParams.

groupId.description: Group whose engine sampled the pressure transition; 'default' in single-group deployments (ADR 0001).

data.description: One proxy group's engine transition (ADR 0001). runtime.stateChanged keeps carrying the top-level aggregate; this event carries per-group detail.
Ephemeral typing indicator (contract 1.15): never persisted, rate limited per account+conversation before it reaches the host lane. The host owns display timeout.

action.description: Upstream typingMessage action; START shows the indicator, STOP clears it immediately.

status.description: State one outgoing message transitioned to; emitted only on a real transition (pending -> sent/unknown/failed, receipts -> delivered/read), never replayed.

deliveredAt.description: Contract 1.32: connector wall-clock ms the delivery receipt that triggered this event stamped the row. Absent on transitions that did not stamp it.

readAt.description: Contract 1.32: connector wall-clock ms the read/viewed receipt that triggered this event stamped the row. Absent on transitions that did not stamp it.

data.description: A view-once message was viewed and its bytes erased (contract 1.38): the body is gone, the media files are deleted, and the row renders as the viewed placeholder. Emitted exactly once per message on the first burn transition — sync-envelope duplicates and replays emit nothing. Deliberately not a message.statusChanged payload: this is the local viewed state, not a peer receipt.

openedAt.description: Connector wall-clock ms the burn stamped the row.

data.description: Local disappearing-message sweep (contract 1.42, §4.41): the sweeper deleted rows whose expire deadline passed in one conversation. messageIds is non-empty and bounded by the sweep batch; a full batch drains immediately, so groups arrive per conversation with no global ordering guarantee. This is the connector-owned expiry of stored history, not a peer receipt and not the upstream burn notice path.

messageIds.description: Row ids removed in this sweep, grouped per conversation.

data.description: Inbound call signaling (contract 1.51, §4.49, capability call-signaling): the engine's callMessage envelope face (official Signal-Desktop RingRTC behavior aligned, AGPL zero-copy) forwarded as a transient event — nothing persists, so a missed delivery is not self-healed (the RingRTC layer re-signals; the connector keeps no call state to reconcile). type is the projected frame family (opaque when only the modern opaque payload rides); payload is the bounded signaling material verbatim — the connector neither parses nor logs it. Delivered to a conversation the connector already resolves; unresolvable signaling drops silently.

callId.description: The 1:1 call identity the frames share; 0 on the modern opaque face (the RingRTC payload carries its own identity).

type.description: The projected frame family: the legacy frame keys, or opaque for the modern Content.callMessage framing.

payload.description: The engine's projected signaling face verbatim: {opaque, urgency, destinationDeviceId} on the modern face, the projected frame under its own key (offer/answer/busy/hangup) or {iceUpdate: [...]} on the legacy faces. The connector never parses the RingRTC content.

data.description: Contract 1.50: optional engine-supplied error facts, pass-through only. PROFILE_UPLOAD_FAILED carries {retryable, textSaved} (the engine's honest partial-success report: the text face landed, the avatar upload failed); the connector never invents or strips keys. Absent on every other error face of engines at this revision.
